trial_name: Sensor-Augmented Pump Therapy for High-Variability T1DM
intervention: Sensor-Augmented Insulin Pump (SAP) vs Multiple Daily Injections (MDI) + CGM
description: Pre-screening protocol modelled on real-world SAP trial designs (STAR 3, SAPiflex, SWITCH studies). Targets adults with Type 1 diabetes mellitus experiencing high glycaemic variability on MDI therapy, as measured by CGM coefficient of variation >= 36%. The 36% CV threshold reflects the AGC consensus definition of high variability (Danne et al., 2017, Diabetes Care). Primary endpoint: reduction in CV% and hypo burden at 26 weeks. Excludes patients already using pump therapy or closed-loop systems.

inclusion_criteria.human_rationale: SAP therapy addresses the erratic insulin kinetics and high CV% characteristic of T1DM. T2DM patients generally have residual beta-cell function and lower variability; including them would dilute the primary endpoint and blur the insulin-physiology mechanism being studied.

This protocol is designed for adults. Paediatric SAP use involves different device hardware, caregiver involvement, and regulatory pathways. STAR 3 and similar adult T1DM SAP trials enrolled from age 18.

Older patients (> 65) may have comorbidities, cognitive factors, or hypoglycaemia unawareness patterns that require separate safety monitoring frameworks. The upper age bound keeps the population homogeneous for the primary CV% endpoint.

A minimum 1-year duration ensures the C-peptide honeymoon period is over and the patient has established T1DM physiology with absolute insulin dependence. This confirms the biological rationale for SAP therapy.

inclusion_criteria.human_label: CGM Coefficient of Variation >= 36% (high glycaemic variability)
inclusion_criteria.human_rationale: CV >= 36% is the AGC/ATTD consensus threshold for 'high variability' (Danne et al., Diabetes Care 2017). Patients below this threshold do not have sufficient variability to demonstrate a meaningful treatment effect from SAP, and would not qualify as having the target phenotype the trial is designed to treat.

exclusion_criteria.human_label: Fewer than 3 severe hypoglycaemic events in monitoring period
exclusion_criteria.human_rationale: Three or more severe hypoglycaemic events suggests hypoglycaemia unawareness that requires immediate clinical intervention (structured hypoglycaemia education, sensor alarm optimisation) before device escalation. Such patients need individualised rather than protocol-driven care.

Patients already achieving TIR >= 70% on MDI are meeting the AGC glycaemic target and would not demonstrate room-for-improvement on the primary endpoint. Enrolling them dilutes the effect size and may expose them to unnecessary device burden without expected benefit.
